tips.comment: Jacquelina is a 6-year-old mare trained by Phil McEntee. She has 6/22 wins on turf (two in today's class 5 grade) and is a two-time winner on today's good to firm ground. She runs today in a class 5, having been running in better races in recent starts. She ran off 75 (last winning mark at Chepstow) just four days ago at Newmarket and led early in a a class 3, only going down by 2 lengths which suggests she may be coming to hand after a disappointing 11/11 at Sandown in penultimate start. Phil McEntee turns his mare out quickly, and he has 31/121 wins from runner if his charge run within 3-5 days from their last run and reside in the top three in the market. Jockey Grace McEntee has ridden more winners for owner Trevor Johnson than any other jockey, with 24 wins (won on Jacquelina in her last four victories). Phil McEntee has provided 56 wins for Trevor Johnson, so they make a great combination and has to be respected in thus grade.
Big chance for Abate today. The horse is ten pounds lower than its last win. Also, a course and distance winner in the past.

Hurt You Never looks poised to strike in a thin looking six runner class 5 handicap that is not as competitive as it may seem at a quick glance was last seen at Haydock 12 days ago where finishing a respectable 3rd/7 currently operating on a mark of 71 that being just 2lb above the mark he won on recently at Hamilton in a similar race he is more than capable of getting the job done of a mark of 71 especially in a race of this nature and he does arrive here in top nick and in very good heart jockey Jack Nicholls takes off a very valuable looking 7lb which only enhances his good looking claims here Adrian Nicholls's inmate must be seriously considered to play a huge role in this class 5 handicap over on the business end

Glory fighter looks ready to strike again here, back to winning mark and this race looks a great chance to get his head back infront. Midgleys sprinters are always dangerous in this grade and with glory fighter drawn well I'm expecting a big front running show.

Spendmore Lane is a 3-year-old filly who makes her stable debut for David Loughnane. She finished 3/8 behind a useful prospect in Westacre, who posted an RPR of 84. Westacre has since won a Group 2-3 in Meydan and posted a career-high RPR of 114. Spendmore Lass bombed on her next start, finishing 8/8, and was quickly put away for the rest of the season.(Eased down as something was amiss) and filly in that last start. Today, after a 253-day break, she sports a first-time hood and Loughnane has had enough time to rectify any niggling issues. Loughnane books Rossa Ryan, which looks significant as he has ridden 52 winners for the stable. Owned by David Armstrong, who has picked up numerous big race winners (10 in total, notably Mayson), and has had 173 winners since 2004 in the UK. She must overcome an Andrew Balding 8-15 chance, but I think she can, as he only has a 7.4% strike rate with juvenile debutantes (65). Balding puts on a first-time hood and is a mere 1/40 wins with 2-year-old juvenile debutantes when sporting a first-time hood/visor, so I'm opposing Secret Sonata with Spendmore Lane.
Good inform stable, well-bred half-sister to Secret Satire and Secret Solace. Looks to have been found a nice opening for her debut.
Good stable, C/D winner 1 year ago. Ran a solid race last time out at Yarmouth when finishing 4th, beaten 1.5 lengths by Zafaan. Serious chance in this field.

Good apprentice rider up, and so the claim will be useful. This cleverly-named horse by Churchill has been responsible for some consistently useful efforts, and it wouldn't take too much improvement in this field to see Inspiring Speeches head them home.

The Pug knows how to get ahead in front, albeit all 3 wins have been on all-weather. But now it drops into classified level, having gone close at Leicester. Tyren Langley is having a season and is a positive jockey booking.

Ex-French trained 5yo, 10 career runs. A decent UK debut four weeks ago when beaten 4L in a class 5 handicap, against rivals rated 62-72. He now drops down into a level weights 0-50 classified stakes. Strong jockey booking for this apprentice riders’ contest, and he can still claim a very useful 5lb.

U S Grant is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Kevin Ryan and is no superstar - 0-7; beaten 3 lengths at Newcastle in April. He's failed to build on that back on turf latest but hung badly left and weakened in the final 110 yards over 1 mile 4 furlongs. Drops in trip today and class (classified stakes) for owner Mrs. Angie Bailey, who has had 89 winners with Kevin Ryan and won numerous pattern races with top-class sprinters such as Astaire 1 (U S Grant is Astaire 1's half-brother) and Brando! Things may start to click now he has seven runs under his belt and is related to smart middle-distance horses Shoshone Warrior 102 and Every Chance 97. Today's drop in trip classified stakes shouldn't hold any fears being relatively unexposed from top connections.

I'm back now after a little break. I don't agree with racing horses in extreme temperatures, so let's try and find some value bets again. Finding decent form in this race is very difficult in this low-grade affair, but at least Mond boasts a close 2nd over this distance at Lingfield on GF ground. He weakened inside the final furlong at Brighton over an extra 2 furlongs, again on GF. Its last run was very poor on good going, but is back on GF today. I personally think he should run a decent race here, and the 18/1 e/w looks the value.

Three career runs for the 2yo colt. An improved run 10 days ago when he was a good staying on 3rd. The runner-up was a good proven yardstick and the winner was a smart 88 rated Appleby trained runner. He has an attractive opening handicap mark of 67 and a strong jockey booking.

All of Daretobedifferent's races have produced winners or good runs in better class contests. Her handicap qualifier at Yarmouth was adequate and she turns up with an opening mark of 70. A reproduction of her first two races puts her in with a very good chance on nursery handicap debut.

A rare jockey booking for the yard and a horse that looks to have a progressive profile for this small outfit. By Mohaather, the distance may get this horse beat, but it's worth a go on this long straight.

Four career runs for the 3yo filly, form 0-223. The form of all three runs this year looks strong. She’s had a nice two month break, strong jockey booking and an attractive opening handicap mark of 75.
Two B Tanned has an exceptional record at the 1m to 1m 1f distance (3 wins from 3 runs, 100%) and a strong 80% win rate on similar going (4 wins from 5 runs).

Veraison won an AW maiden last summer and was a decent third on the return from a break in April when second up in handicaps. She comes into today off the same mark but having had wind surgery and gets Hollie Doyle to help out while stepping up to C4 for only her second run on turf after being fourth in a C4 maiden at Newbury last summer.

Mrs Trump won an 18-runner class 6 at Thirsk last time by a nose and has gone up just three pounds. She is reasonably well handicapped and goes well at this track. At 11/4 or bigger, there is some juice in the price. Stable-switching and handicap-dropping Chasing Gold rates a danger, having benefited from wind surgery recently.

Nottingham Racecourse must be thrilled. 28 runners in the last 6 races, wow! The selection wins very infrequently and under no circumstances can be called a good thing. But racing below its last winning weight, it must have a definite chance, and I will be surprised if it does not contest.

With Mrs Trump penalised 3lb after a recent win, this race seems to be between Four Adaay, weighted to go well but always seems to find one too good, and King of the Jungle, who could be that one. Also weighted to go close, but a 7lb claimer on board may help this gelding get his head in front.

Chasing Gold has not been in the money yet but changed yards last month and came straight in with a not far away fourth at 5f off a 60 after wind surgery. As I always expect more when second up, he could improve on that while keeping Rossa Ryan in the saddle and dropping to a 58 with a step up to 6f.

Only 6 runners and the Mark Usher-trained Arlecchinos Gift is a huge price. Admittedly, he is a hard one to predict. However, he has 9 wins and 11 places from 60 starts. The 6-year-old gelding has eased a pound to 60, and there is not a great deal between all six runners. He seems largely overpriced at around 28s. He won off 62 at Wolverhampton last September and off a mark of 60 at Kempton in February. His career is littered with good performances when you might least expect them.

Louie The Legend is a 3yo gelding trained by Dylan Cunha and ridden by Ray Dawson. He won on good to soft over 7f at Chepstow last August, opening on a mark of 77. Things haven't gone to plan since and he was subsequently gelded. He runs today off a career low handicap mark of 64 and showed some signs of a revival when finishing 4/9 last time out at Pontefract over 1m 2f behind some experienced older handicappers who had amassed some 18 wins. 'Prominent behind clear leader, briefly led over 1f out, weakened inside final furlong, lost third final strides.' Today he drops 2f and runs in a class 6 for the first time under Ray Dawson, who replaces an inexperienced amateur. With conditions looking favourable, Louie The Legend is my short-priced banker of the day.
Still lightly raced, this 3-year-old, and the drop back to a mile may suit better today. It's always best to catch these smaller stables when hitting some decent form like this one has as of late.

The handicapper seems to have most of these tapped and doesn't seem to want to relent yet. A horse dropping in grade could then well be the answer. Selection is COEUR JAUNE, who has been running in class 5 handicaps (6 today) and was only beaten 1.5 lengths last time off 63, same mark today but ease in grade should be enough.
Read All About It looks of interest here on handicap debut, given the form so far, and ultimately has looked the most convincing in this company.

Lightly raced maiden who looks to be moving in the right direction and enjoyed arguably his best effort last time out when 4th of 10 at Beverley back in April of this year. With a dropped mark, he does have a chance.

Very well-bred 2-year-old filly who should be ready first time here to run well and could have too much class for the five rivals in this race. The trainer does well with this type, and although this 5f may be a sharp enough test, she should be strong late on being bred for further.
Two nicely bred newcomers top the market in this novice stakes and I feel it’s the selection that will be more suited by this 5f trip.

No show in first 2 starts, but they were @ much higher level than this class 5 and selection is a half sister to 4 winners. Good jockey up and very good trainer who has a good record in this race, is tops here with his 2yo's @ 20 percent last 5 seasons, making current 28/1 very good Ew value in the race top 2.
Karl Burke has brought Dunkeld Dreamer along with nurseries in mind. That in itself gives rise to huge hopes in the first race at Beverley today.
Poor race this is. Chance taken on the horse that beat 10 rivals home, 1 pound better off for that class 3 seller at York. Treat with caution.

Three career runs for the 3yo filly. She was 5th of 13 in a selling stakes last time out, beaten 3L but it was a decent £13K contest with plenty of runners around her rated 70+. She’s now making her handicap debut off a 60 mark against rivals rated 45-56.
Monica's Lad steps up in trip, a move likely to suit after showing promise. Cheekpieces go on for focus. Yard won this last year. Top course trainer. Could surprise.
Quirke On Parole did a good job here last month when winning on GF off a 53. He returns today just 2 lbs heavier on a similar trip and going, but does get Kevin Stott this time. I expect more today.

Unusually tricky Class 6. Michael Dodds, trainer of Homeland, is rather like Appleby for me. An excellent trainer, but I have a hell of a hard job telling when it's on. Homeland ran a decent 3rd last time, and although yet to find the winning post, it looks to be improving and has a good chance. Fair draw. Owned by a pair surname Moses. If they could part the Red Sea, should have an advantage.

Three runs this year for the 4yo. He was aimed too high two weeks ago and is in much calmer waters now. Plenty to like about his return run when finishing a good second over this 10f C/D. That form is working out well and the selection is a couple of lb lower now.

Declan Carroll's Time Tells All remains a maiden after sixteen starts, but he’s a son of Sea The Stars and a half-brother to Group 1 winning Homeless Songs, who was also trained by Dermott Weld. He moved from the stable after being sold for a sizable fee of 45,000 GNS, so he should be doing better than he has so far. Today he is down in trip and grade with what’s potentially his optimum conditions. He can go well.

It's been a rather frustrating season with several eye-catching runs but no wins. Eye-catching again last time when 3rd at Pontefract in an amateur riders' race when getting going far too late. Drops in class and drops a furlong in distance. Each way only.
Not too far at all behind Quirke On Parole only a few weeks back, and I just can't understand why such a big price is available. Happy to take the odds here.

4yo filly by Kessaar, one of two runners in this race for Ollie Pears, has won 4 of 21 races. Interesting here returning from wind surgery. Handicap mark has dropped from a high of 74 to 61 now. Could be up to this if the wind surgery has had a positive effect. Harry Russell rides.

I'm surprised Havachoc is the likely outsider in the betting here after an improver's third when produced right-handed for the first time. Runs on another right-handed course here, and that might be the key to the roan gelding by Havana Gold.
Course and distance winner last time, pulling away nicely in the closing stages to win with something in hand. Just 11 days ago and out on a higher mark, but might just be ahead of the handicapper.

Mick & David Easterby's Carolus Magnus was an eyecatcher in a competitive big-field seven-furlong handicap at York on Yorkshire Cup day last season. He met in-running trouble after a poor start and backed that up with another decent effort at Chester eight days later, beating 12 rivals when finishing sixth. He gets in here off a low mark of 66 and could be ready after the best part of a year to do himself justice under Joanna Mason.
Kracking has a good and convincing form. If not the winner, he will definitely be thereabouts in the finish for top 3 or top 4 finish.

Ran a strong race here last week over this exact course and distance, finishing a close third in a better run Class 5. He's a proven Beverley performer, drops into a slightly easier race, and is well drawn to sit handy. Off the same mark and clearly in form, he looks a lively contender at double-figure odds.

Is getting on now, but retains their form well and good run in this class Lto when coming 5/9 beaten 3 lengths over 7f @ Thirsk. Retains that mark of 63 here, is a C/D winner, good jockey up and very shrewd dual trainer is best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons @ 17 percent, making current 9/1 very good Ew value in the race.

Among the 6 C&D winners in this fiercely competitive field, but currently not in the best of form. However, the last run was back in January of this year. It's the current mark that is most appealing, which is 4 lbs lighter than the last winning mark.

The 4yo ran well in the spring, with a win and followed that with a very close 3rd of 15 - same mark today. The 1st and 2nd from that handicap are both rated much higher now. He has been lit up in his last two starts, way too keen, and eased at halfway. However, he has a good jockey booking and if he settles he can go well at a big price.

Just three starters here. Charging Thunder was 3rd in Newcastle two weeks ago in a field of 20. That was a good performance, and it was a 150,000 pounds race. I think he's the one to beat today. The jockey is still Harry Davies.

The 5yo ran well two weeks ago in a decent AW contest, a first try over this 16f trip, he was a good staying on 4th and clear of the rest. He was racing off a 7lb higher mark as recently as May. The fav looks a nice prospect but the 3yo did have a hard race 10 days ago, a 5lb higher mark and is now taking on older runners for the first time.

Better form from the 5yo in his last two races, only losing out late on, and he seems in good shape. He has been up against better rivals than what he now faces in this 0-55 handicap. He was rated way higher last summer.

Only 1-25 with that victory coming early in his career with Archie Watson, but seems to have found his level for Tina Jackson now and went close off this mark at Catterick in May. Not one for maximum faith for sure, but should be capable of going close in this weak event.

Michael Herrington's Araifjan was once rated as high as 78, his last winning mark was one of 59 when he made all on Chelmsford all-weather surface over six furlongs in 2023. He has shown glimpses of form, and his best performance in recent times came when finishing third over this C&D off a two lb higher mark than the one of 46 he carries here in May. He was a bit unlucky that day, having been caught behind a wall of horses and forced to switch around them while the first two were already away. If he can recapture that form, he'll have a good chance of winning this.

Well-drawn IFONLYTHEYCUDTALK is considered here. Despite the unspectacular form of late, he's back at the site of his last win and at a rock-bottom mark to boot. The mid-division finishes of late could be upgraded before long, and there'll be some front runners to try and chase down here. Hopefully, he finds the gap and gets involved.
CD, who is suited by a stiff five furlongs. Not the best of draws, but is now on a very good-looking handicap mark and looks a strong each-way possibility at least.

Jack of Clubs will be hoping the rain reaches Beverley. He won this race last season on soft ground from a handicap mark of 55. Today, he races from a mark of 52. He hasn't shown much form so far this season, but the easier ground can see him improve today.

16th of 18 over 6 furlongs in a race where the field split at Thirsk last time, but 2nd of 3 in the group she raced in. Eased a pound in the ratings and could be suited by the drop back to 5 furlongs.

In a wide-open Class 6 handicap, an each-way chance is taken on the Stella Barclay-trained Sir Benedict at a decent price of around 12/1. The 7-year-old Dandy Man gelding has 6 wins and 17 places from 65 starts. He gets in off joint bottom weight with a mark of just 46, and if he puts his best hoof forward, he could trouble the judge in this company.
Been pitching in pretty decent races for the level, and although the finishing distances have been great, each time this horse was stalking up others. Has to be in with a shot here.

I think the Michael Dods yard has finally turned the corner, given how well his runners have performed over the last ten days. He's represented here by Brazilian Belle, who has been steadily improving with racing. Her second to the big improver, Lord Roxby, last time reads well. She was clear of the third that day and can go one better this time.
Just didn't end up getting home on last start and you would think that this horse definitely has to be in with a strong shout here.

Backing Glorious Kitty, the lightly raced 3-year-old Cotai Glory filly trained by Michael & David Easterby, in tomorrow’s Thirsk Racecourse Handicap over 5f. She’s been running well of late, placing third on the AW at Wolverhampton in March and fourth at Epsom in June, before closing the Galtres Stakes meeting with a third over 6f at Hamilton. That run confirmed she handles quick turf and sprint trips. Rated around 73, she’s now dropping back in trip after those solid efforts and lands in this smaller field of 8 runners, set to be ridden by Billy Garritty. His positive, forward style should allow her to tuck in just off the pace before launching a strong late surge up Thirsk’s short straight. With a career-best still in her locker, Glorious Kitty looks to be very nicely treated and could prove over-priced around 8/1??'10/1.

Marajito gained its first win last time out at Redcar with an impressive run off a mark of 68 in a 5f event. It has a 7lb penalty tonight to contend with, but it looks worth following this in-form sprinter again here under jockey David Allan.
Shaped well on turf/handicap debut 3 runs back and now comes here a pound lower. Drops down in grade and has a 3lb claimer, lightening his load by another 3lb. Big chance.

Should be a straight fight between Langholm and WITHOUT DELAY. Both horses are rated 2 points clear of the third, and with Tracy Waggot's horses 'running to form' percentage at 70%, her horse is the choice.
Seems to save his best for Thirsk and has been looking to hold some of the form recently. Looks like a good each-way price to side with here.
Won over the extended 7 furlongs here on penultimate start and didn’t get a clear run when 4th of 11 over that same trip 11 days ago. Should be just as effective over this slight drop in trip.
A weak-looking handicap where My Honey B looks great value at 14/1. She wasn't beaten far at Newcastle last time and continues to drop in the handicap. Today's drop in trip is another plus.

Backing Korroor, the 4-year-old Kodiac gelding trained by Julie Camacho, in tomorrow’s Ideal Conference Venue Handicap (7f, Class 6). He arrives in sound form off the back of a solid 3rd of 8 at Nottingham on 12 June, finishing strongly over 6f and marking himself fit for this return to 7 furlongs. Previously, he scored twice over this trip on Tapeta??'including a comfortable win at Newcastle on 20 March, racing prominently and responding well under Tom Kiely??'Marshall. That return to turf saw him run well after a wind operation, performing under pressure and suggesting he’s capable of stepping forward.
Rated around 47, Korroor is well handicapped and stepping back into calmer waters against a decent but not strong field of 13 runners. With a visor left on and race-fit already, his versatile running style??'able to lead or race prominently??'and consistent form on both AW and turf point to him being well-placed to hit the frame. Expect him to settle with cover before launching a late surge up Thirsk’s straight.
At likely odds of 18/1??'20/1, Korroor offers genuine each-way value as an improving horse on a workable mark.

Very disappointing last time in a C6 race, but had shown promise on his previous start, which has thrown up multiple winners. The last race was about 6 weeks ago, and this stable has hit a rich vein of form since then. So, racing off bottom weight today, he can spring a surprise.

Decent Neck finished 2nd place at Brighton on first time out since a 113-day break. Showed good character on 2nd race at Kempton on previous break and should strip fitter again to be in the mix here. Prices suggest an open race and has a favorable high draw.

Races don't get much weaker than this, and this horse has a huge chance on her 2nd place finish on her penultimate start. The horse at least showed that she has some gears to run on to gain 2nd, and such is the lack of depth in this race, that the effort there is more than enough to be involved in the finish here. She's much less exposed than most of these, which have already shown their limitations, and there's a decent jockey booking too, so she should be a single-figure price in my opinion. I'd have her nearer to a 7/1 shot.
They are dropping this one back down in trip and grade with the same 3 lbs claimer on board. A good value each way bet.

I would have liked to have seen this one in a handicap race, but I will try a small each way anyway. The trainer clearly had work to do after the first 3 runs on the all-weather from Dec-Feb, all over 7f, as it couldn't live with the pace. After nearly 5 months off, a new trip and a change of tactics saw MFC leading from the front over 1m 2f, but faded badly with about 2.5f to go and came last. The fact that it was running with the others proved to me that work had been done and there seemed to be more speed now, but probably the wrong trip and race fitness were the problem. Down to this all but 8f's today with first-time cheekpieces and I hope the same front-running tactics could see a more competitive horse today and could hold on for a place.

Was a maiden hurdle winner 3 runs back and not been entirely disgraced on the flat last 2 runs. Fast run race here would suit, good jockey up and very good dual trainer is best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons @ 17 percent with a Lsp of 15.33, making current 18/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Six horses are making their debut tomorrow, and he is among them. He is also the half-sister to the useful winner over 6f, Dreams of Reality. While the sire, Ardad (IRE), has a strike rate that is not what we are looking for, he does have the ability to bag big wins.

Shiela's Well looked to burn up a bit of energy at the start of the last race, having to track over from the wide draw. Now in a better position and with a convincing profile, expect a decent run here.

Miss Yorkshire has been running well, placing on all 3 starts on turf and on the all-weather. She is upped to 1m today, and it shouldn't be a problem. She should go close in this class 5 contest off a mark of 70.

Liberty Bird lines up today in a Class 5 Apprentice Handicap with Archie Young aboard. She's shown her best form over this trip on good-to-firm ground, with two previous wins at this distance. The jockey has partnered her recently for a solid effort. While recent runs have been disappointing, she returns to more suitable conditions and remains attractively handicapped.

Sinj has shown strong consistency with three placings in four starts (0% win rate but 75% place rate), all at 6f on turf. Her latest run at Newbury (13th, beaten 17l) was disappointing, but she did too much too soon, suggesting she can bounce back if ridden more conservatively.

Went off too fast latest over 6f, fading out and getting well beaten. But worth trying the drop back to 5f. Can continue progress having been runner-up twice previously. Billy Loughnane back in the saddle is a plus. Should go well on handicap debut.
Dakota Dawn has been brought along with handicaps in mind and here is his first handicap. Confident he will run well and hopefully take a win in his first nursery handicap for John Quinn.
Seems to be coming into form. Ran second 10 days ago, not really putting it down in the last 100 yards. However, I hope that was a one-off. Kevin Ryan is a great trainer of anything equine.

Twilight Jazz is a 5-year-old mare trained by Mike Sowersby and ridden by Paul Mulrennan. She is a two-time winner but doesn't come here in the best of form. However, there are some positives: she is 2/19 wins on turf and has won on today's good to firm ground. Five out of six of her best-placed finishes on turf, including wins, have come on good to firm ground. She seems to come to hand around this time of year, with five out of six best-placed finishes on turf coming in the month of July, with one in August. In her last attempt in a classified stakes on turf, she finished 2/7, beaten by 1/2 length by Time Tested (49), a 4-year-old who has won three times since and is currently rated 72. Sowersby is a dual-purpose trainer, predominantly in the NH sphere, but does have the occasional winner on the flat. He is 4/49 wins and 10/49 placed since 2023, showing a healthy LSP of £109, winning with a 125-1, 20-1, 5-1, and 4- 1 (Paul Mulrennan back in March at Newcastle. Each way play with conditions in her favour and a significant jockey booking.

The third at Newmarket last time looks decent, and a repeat of that can win this race. That Newmarket race came after a break, so should be even fitter tonight. Steps back down in trip to the distance of the Wolverhampton win in the spring. Fine young jockey who is good value for the three-pound claim.

Gastronomy ran consistently, finishing 5th, beaten 1¼l off a mark of 64 over 1m 4f at Newcastle last time. His 10% win rate at the 1m 6f distance (1 win from 10 runs) and 9.09% win rate on similar going (1 win from 11 runs) show he’s suited to the conditions.

Celestial Reigns is back on the level for the first time since joining Micky Hammond after progressive spell hurdling for yard and the ex-Irish 4yo is taken to make a successful handicap debut in this small field stayers contest.
He was rather unfortunate to have been brought down 2 out on stable debut at Sedgefield having looked likeliest winner. He was given a bit much to do when 4th/5 back there nto and beaten only 2l. He made it third time lucky at the track when narrowly seeing off Solent Gateway on run-in having jumped better than the fav in that maiden hurdle. The form was franked with Solent Gateway winning both starts since. Finally, Celestial Reign was just touched off final strides to Terrorise at Cartmel and that form was also franked with Terrorise bolting up on the flat at York last weekend.
Celestial Reign was winless for Joseph O’Brien but closest he came was nose 2nd in Sligo maiden over 1m3f. As 2m4f hurdles winner for current connections, he's going to find today’s 1m6f on the level more adequate. He’s rated 110 over hurdles with probably more to come so rating of 69 in this sphere looks fine.

Comes from top trainer Willie Mullins and has found itself in a smaller, weaker field of runners. Came second on seasonal debut, 7 lengths behind the leader, so probably needed the run out. Steps up in trip by 4 furlongs, and the jockey gets a 7-pound claimer, both of which are bonuses for the horse. Looks to be a consistent type, and improvement is likely. Should get off the mark today.

Horse that likes being stepped up in trip after finishing 2nd at Ballinrobe over 16.5f won well at Wexford over 21f by 4L 11 days ago . Steps up an extra 1f again today but J.Kennedy is out the plate & 7Lb claimer takes the ride , slight worry about 11 day turnaround .
Won well on hurdles debut in May. Disappointing on next run, but ground didn't suit. Gets good ground today and upped in trip, which should be a plus.
Fitness is taken on trust but is not normally an issue for a Willie Mullins newcomer. I don’t think he would have named one Closutton unless it was useful, so it can make a winning start.

Closutton is very nicely bred and could be useful for the Willie Mullins stable but backing a horse at odds on first time out when there are promising alternatives looks a risk and the comments in the Racing Post from the stable were that she was decent but not a world beater. Walks The Talk looks to have a decent chance to upset the odds. She bolted up in a point to point at Dromahane and ran a nice first race under rules behind a very good horse. She may have needed that a bit as it was her first run since October and John McConnell has a very good record in bumpers, so she looks to have a good each way chance. She is also very nicely bred and open to plenty of improvement.

Did not run that badly on debut run, as they were hampered 4f out and then stayed on well final 2f to come 6/12 beaten 16.5 lengths in a similar level NHF race over 2.1 miles @ Bellestown. Entitled to come on for that run/experience, step up to this 2.3 miles should suit and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 20/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Elana Osario is a 4-year-old filly trained by P Twomey. She finally got her head in front on her penultimate start, having shown a lot of early promise. She stepped up in trip latest and posted a career-high RPR of 87 when just failing to get up to the progressive filly Heather and lost by a head on her handicap debut - clear of the rest by some 4.5l. There should be more to come, being a sixth foal and a full sister to five individual winners, three of which posted RPRs of 109, 109, and 117, and out of a Listed winning dam who won on good to soft (yielding today, which is essentially good to soft). Colin Keane rides, and his filly also brings course form to the table, finishing runner-up to an A P O'Brien trained Get (77) by 2.25 lengths on heavy ground over CD. Get is now rated 100, and she won't be inconvenienced by any further rain. The welterweight of 10 stone is the only issue, but she must have a big chance.on form and pedigree.
A maiden winner in May and two good runs since. 3/7 last time out when up in trip as BF, badly hampered that day and can do better. Regular jockey GM Ryan back on board.

Clearly goes well with cut in the ground as they showed again Lto, when coming 2/15 beaten 4.5 lengths in a slightly lesser handicap over 1.1 miles @ Leopardstown. That was only their 4th run so clearly should have a lot of improvement in them, only 1lb higher here, pieces on first time, good jockey up (D McMonagle prefers stable favourite in the race) and top trainer best here numerically last 5 seasons, making current 14/1 solid Ew value in the race.
Has won her last two races and has already beaten five of today's rivals previously. Should make a bold bid for the hat-trick.

Jasmine Affanalis is a 3-year-old filly trained by David Marnane and ridden by Luke McAteer. She was raised 2lb by the Irish handicapper from 53-55 for a promising 2/15 at Limerick on her penultimate start when going down by 3 lengths to In The Minus (52 received 1lb), a horse that has subsequently finished a neck runner-up in a claimer, posting a career-high RPR of 68. Jasmine Affanalis was slightly disappointing on her last start, but there were excuses: 'Midfield, switched right and ran on from 2f out, hampered on inner inside final furlong, kept on (jockey said filly was hampered a furlong down).' Luke and David generally make a formidable combination in handicaps on runners who are sent off at 10-1 or less, with 28/90 wins showing a healthy LSP of £97.12. If Jasmine Affanalis avoids trouble, she could be very well handicapped given the form she showed on her penultimate start at Limerick. Chance!

Mon St Michel has been aimed at this race since the start of the year with Pat Smullen's teenage son riding, Paddy Smullen. The track will be alight for this race. They want to see the deceased jockey's son come home with his first winner. If he does, 'the roof comes off the stand' with the noise! A very well-bred horse can win this comfortably and land our NAP. After all, this horse was four lengths behind Kyprios in the Levmoss Stakes at Leopardstown two months ago!

ROYAL HOLLOW has been placed in two races from four starts also won two hurdle races at 2m 1f second over 1m 7f at Leopardstown on her latest outing last month dropped in trip to 1m 6f should suit and could well be able to go one better and win this race

Slightly intriguing runner for Charles Byrnes who has trained a decent stayer in the past (Run For Oscar). 40-1 winner of a handicap hurdle over 2 miles at Limerick in October, otherwise very little form to note. Some staying potential in pedigree on the dam's side. Only five years old, with Clive Cox as a youngster, placed twice. Interesting in that he ran five days ago and could potentially come on for that outing. 7lbs claimer Glen Norris retains the ride.

Finished in the frame on 7 of 10 outings for previous stable. Got no run from a poor draw on debut for this yard at the Curragh last time. Now down a pound and top rider on board, should be tough to beat.

Not too sure she enjoyed the soft going last time out, and it was also her first run of the season. It doesn't look like a great race, to be honest, with the favorite having its first run for a year, and the second favorite didn't look much last time out. But we have two runners having their first race as well and could be anything. Sister Lily did improve from last year's run, and with fitness and better ground, she should improve again.

Fool Me Once has shown steady progression, with a strong 2nd (beaten 4½l) over 2m 6f at this course in his latest outing. His 0% win rate but 28.57% place rate in hurdle races (2 placings from 7 starts) and suitability for a stiff test make him a strong contender.

Ollie La Ba Ba won a maiden hurdle over two miles six furlongs at this meeting a year ago. He started chasing this season but fell at the first fence in his second chase and has been switched back to hurdles. He could have every chance of getting his second win.
Divilabother is still looking for its first win after thirteen outings, but this looks to be a perfect opportunity after finishing second last time.

Portarlington has slipped to an attractive mark after winning three on the bounce last year. Ran a better race last time out at Roscommon. The jockey won two of those three wins and has a recent win to his name with a win at Bellewstown. This doesn't look like a strong race and is there for the taking.
Order Of The Dance would probably have finished further up the field had it not been hampered in its last race. It had two seconds previously.
Chance taking on the horse that ran well last time out in a Class 5. Went off big odds then, stepping up in class but 5 pounds better off than last race.
Not seen for 11 months and completely unproven at this trip but has shown ability , her yard are in good form and have booked a top amateur jockey. Each way claims in a weak race.

His two runs this year suggest he has improved for a winter break, and he may be ready to shed his maiden tag today. His fourth place finish in a Sligo claimer last month probably constituted a career best, and a reproduction of that form now returned to handicap company off a career low mark might just be good enough.
Failed to impress on chase debut last time. Reverts back to hurdles. Won over course and distance here on penultimate start and is 5lb higher here. Chance as he won easy enough on that last win.

Noel Kelly's mare showed her first piece of worthwhile form over CD in May and then possibly surpassed that when finishing just over 6 lengths behind her well-gambled stablemate Nakassama at Hexham 38 days ago over 2 furlongs shorter. She was unfancied on both occasions and was probably there as a companion on her Northumberland jaunt. I don't think she'll be unfancied here over her right trip and 6 pounds lower than last time.
They are stepping this one back up in trip slightly with a 7 lbs claiming jockey booking/change. A good value each way bet for the 4 places available.

Shark Hanlon's 7 year old French Gelding FIREWORKS has gotten under my skin more than he should have & now I can't shake the fact I think he may have a small each way chance here. This Son of KINGSMAN ran as well as to be expected at Wexford 48 days ago when coming off a mammoth 517 day sabbatical yes he jumped a bit rusty (which was to be expected) but I thought he ran ok & was making a bit of headway 3 from the lollypop before tiring & prior to this there was another run off a break (albeit not as significant) so I'm keen to see how this French Charge fares now (hopefully) rust free. This lad has dropped another 2lbs and gets the services of in form 5lb claimer Shane O'Callaghan who has a very impressive 75% place strike rate this past month. Trainer has a 35.29% place strike rate here in Northern Ireland the past year. Certainly not one to put the mortgage on but the curiosity has me & at 22/1 I'll allow it.

Yes, the form line is far from inspiring and deserves to be at long odds. But sometimes a change of scenery can work the oracle for a horse who has been found wanting in a bigger yard. Rosemary Connors now has this mare, and this is her first run for Rosie. Looked useful at Thurles a season back on debut over bigger fences. In her only run over them this time, she was prominent but then found wanting and wasn't persevered with. A repeat of that effort at Thurles could bring her into contention.
Won on the flat last time off a mark of 65. Last run over jumps off 94 in May when placed and is allowed in here off the same mark. Very much well in on flat mark. Decent chance.

Ar Nos Na Gaoithe was pulled from a race yesterday so strong signs that trainer has decided to run him today. Has been racing consistently well and should feature if running to same level. Strong traveller who went close here last time out. NAP

Enchanted Garden has won 3 of her 9 starts the last coming at Leopardstown off a mark of 72 in April. She has been unplaced since off 77 at Curragh in May and 74 last month but now down to 73 with Jack Cleary taking off 5lbs she looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer

Harry The Rogue is a 4-year-old gelding trained by Andrew Slattery. He has won over 1m here and at Naas this year and continues in fine form year-to-date, rising from a mark of 50 (Naas win) to a current mark of 72. He is both consistent and progressive. He posted a career-high RPR of 74 last time out off 67 and has been raised a further 5lb when beaten by a head, finishing 2/16 by another progressive sort in Finsceal Annie over 7f, at Leopardstown one of Irelands flagship tracks a horse who had previously won over CD. The winner opened on a mark of 50 and now rated 78, a 28lb improvement from the 4- year-old filly. Todays step back up to a mile seems the right move and Sam Coen knows this fella well having won on him at Killarney and Naas amSlattery remaina in good form (7/33) with his My Girl Sioux battling gamely to fend off challenge after challenge at Navan to make to land a second win in a row just yesterday.
Has been very consistent and did well to finish fourth of fifteen at Leopardstown last time out after missing the break. Can make amends here with more luck at the start.
Goldrush Kid showed promise with a recent fourth in a tougher handicap. Dropping in grade here, he's well-placed for a strong performance. The anticipated rain should also be in his favour.

I feel there is a plot brewing here for Tony Martin's French 5 year old Gelding ZUZUKEL & to my untrained eye she was held back a little when last seen on the turf. This Son of the Mighty FRANKEL was plodding on fair enough through the juice filled turf at Limerick(1f Soft) on penultimate with 2nd,3rd & 4th placed going on to win since. Obviously the fact that Top jockey Colin Keane remains in the plate is a big plus & certainly shows this yards intentions. Trainer has a 46.67% place strike this past month. Back to the turf for handicap debut here with the underfoot sludge from a pedigree point of view should work in his favour. I could be wrong (and quite possibly am) but I think this charge will be let of the leesh a bit sooner (if they even adopt hold up tactics that is) I'm happy to be wrong & at 14/1 currently ill side with this French Lad each way.

Ronan Whelan for P J Fahey here and at the odds I quite like this horse's chances, given that he actually won last time out but was then relegated to second. Big improver at Down Royal and the yielding ground underfoot should suit perfectly.

BRAINS wins when he likes and is difficult to predict when it’s his going day, but there’s a few factors here to suggest he might go close today .. he’s a 13 times distance winner so no issues with the trip, the going has come up soft here overnight and he’s a winner and placed on it and he’s back down to just 1lb above his last winning mark.. the draw isn’t ideal in 12 and he’s a 9 y/o so he’s vulnerable.. but he could easily outrun these odds..

He's a big outsider and understandably so given that his form took a downward turn in the second half of last year. His first two runs of 2024 were quite promising however, a fourth over today's course and distance then finishing third at Fairyhouse sixteen days later. He may be best caught fresh on that limited evidence, and he's eight pounds lower today. Highly speculative but potentially very rewarding at huge odds.

Zanahiyr is taken to score for Gordon Elliott (SR 20%). Ran fourth behind stablemate Mordor over course and distance on last run back in May. Likely better for a break of 63 days since then and any rain will be a positive for his chances. Grade 2 winning hurdler in the past. Reliable, talented stayer dropped 1 pound in the handicap and looks decently handicapped here on a mark of 76 (9 stone 5 pounds). 8yo by Nathaniel. Declan McDonogh up again.
One old-timer I regularly put up but also gets regularly withdrawn is Lord Erskine, which if goes, could put this lot away if on that good day. Nibbles for it already.

He's a well-bred Dubawi gelding who has shown ability over this distance and mark, previously winning on the Flat and twice over the hurdles. He looks a stayer in the making, while the stable booking looks positive. On balance, the best on form in this field.

I fancy this horse will make the frame in this race. Last time out, it ran a very eye-catching run. It ran on from the back in a Curragh 2-mile handicap that suited the front runners, and this horse was the only one making ground on the placed horses. Today, it gets its ground and is 2lb lower than its last winning mark.
There are a few with good chances in this race and I am going to side with Lady Pagasa who has placed in the last 4 races and will be fresh from a lay off.

Piatra Neamt is lightly raced, showing promise on debut, and steps up in trip, which looks likely to suit based on pedigree and the trainer's comment saying they needed a longer distance. SM Duffy doesn't carry a flashy record, but this could be a sharp placement in a weak field where most rivals are thoroughly exposed. Yielding to soft ground on this distance should help a late-running type like this settle.
